about: The NPU's model server for each vendor, as data (NPU-VENDORS.md beside this file says why each was chosen and what is unverified): how detection tells the vendor and generation, the server's pinned download, how it installs, the models it pulls, its port, caps and timeouts. The node part's npu-vendors.ts reads it; setup installs from it. A server or model is changed here, with its pinned size and SHA-256, and released as a kit version. Sizes in bytes, times in milliseconds. %LOCALAPPDATA% and %USERPROFILE% are expanded; {tools} is the tools home (toolsHome), {port} the server's port, {model} a model's id.

idleStop.about: When the NPU's servers stop after a quiet spell (the keeper, keeper.ts), unless config.json's npuIdleStopMinutes says otherwise. The same rule stops a graphics card's llama.cpp servers on such a PC when the card shares the PC's memory (under 2 GB of its own: integrated graphics, whose models hold the PC's own memory), unless config.json's gpuIdleStopMinutes says otherwise, from cardColdStartMs: llama.cpp b11669's longest start from the disk cache to the first answer on an Intel Core Ultra 5 225U's graphics, 5.4 s for Qwen3-VL-4B with its projector (3.8 to 5.2 s for Qwen3-4B, 1.6 to 2.9 s for the embedding model), rounded up. A card with memory of its own keeps rules.json's keeper.gpuIdleStopMinutes. On a PC with less than smallPcGb of memory (Windows shows a 16 GB PC as 15.3 to 15.9; the next common size is 24 or 32), each route's own minutes per kind (its idleStop.minutes); on a bigger PC, rules.json's keeper.npuIdleStopMinutes, as before. A route's minutes are coldStartTimes times its cold start (idleStop.coldStartMs: stopped to the first answer), so waking it again costs at most a twentieth of the quiet spell it ends, and never under floorMinutes, so the pauses in a conversation, or between an agent's rounds, never pay it. None of the three servers can drop its model and keep running: GenieX's --keepalive unloads it, but the process keeps some 340 MB from every load until it exits; OpenVINO Model Server started with --source_model can't unload one (only its config-file mode can); FastFlowLM documents no unload. So the keeper stops the server, holding the NPU's turn, and the next request starts it again in its own turn.

snapdragon-x.label: Snapdragon X / X Plus / X Elite (Hexagon v73)

serverPin.basis: GenieX 0.9.3 (QAIRT 2.50, llama.cpp e467e5b) runs both of its models: its Qwen3-VL-2B through the llama.cpp plugin, with the signed Hexagon v73 code it carries (libggml-htp-v73.so), and its fallback, AI Hub's current Qwen3-VL-4B build for the X Elite (v0.65.0, built with QAIRT 2.50.0 on 2026-10-21), each measured on it (the basis below). It gets Castellan's build of the plugin, as the X2 does (the route's versions). 0.8.0, the route's own, carries no v73 code fit for a picture on the Hexagon (it reads them grey there), and AI Hub's earlier 4B build, which the kit pinned for the X Elite, is no longer published. The installer's size and SHA-256 as GitHub and GenieX's own .sha256 publish them, checked on a download (2026-10-23)

fallback.basis: No X Elite has run the Qwen3-VL-2B yet: only its v73 code, played on the X2 Elite. So where it doesn't download, or setup's test fails (an answer, and the red test picture seen red), setup sets up the route's Qwen3-VL-4B on the same GenieX in its place, tested as before, and the X Elite keeps chat and pictures on the NPU. AI Hub's current X Elite build of the 4B, played on the X2 Elite with GenieX 0.9.3 (its own data folder naming the X Elite's chip to AI Hub, 2026-10-23): its first answer 8.1 s after the start, 41.1 tokens written a second, 22 of 24 quality items, 3 of npu-bench's 4 pictures right and the red picture seen red, the processor 1.02 cores busy while writing, a 5.92 GB working set. The keeper's refresh keeps a PC on it; setup run again tries the 2B first.

snapdragon-x.basis: Its models, in the route's Qwen3-VL-4B's place from kit 2.101.0 (the owner's choice: the 2B had been better all round on the X2): Qwen3-VL-2B (Q4_0 GGUF) through GenieX's llama.cpp plugin, its language model and its pictures on the Hexagon. Qualcomm AI Hub builds no Qwen3-VL-2B for the X Elite's chip (its release assets, v0.65.0, have only this universal GGUF, for GenieX's llama.cpp plugin), and GenieX 0.9.3 carries llama.cpp's signed Hexagon code for every Hexagon from v73 (libggml-htp-v73.so to -v81.so, and its catalog). Played on the X2 Elite with GenieX 0.9.3 and Castellan's build of its plugin (GGML_HEXAGON_ARCH=v73, which llama.cpp's Hexagon backend reads in place of the one it finds; its log showed the v73 library loaded, and the pictures read on the Hexagon's second session), 2026-10-23, on a private port in the NPU's turn: its first answer 2.2 s after the start, 71.2 tokens written a second, 21 of 24 quality items, npu-bench's 4 pictures right in a median 413 ms and setup's red picture seen red, the processor 0.05 cores busy while writing, a 2.69 GB working set after the pictures; with the X2's own v81 code, 2.0 s, 72.9, 22 of 24, 4 of 4 in 398 ms, 0.07 cores and 2.68 GB. That is v73 code on an X2's NPU, never an X Elite's speed or memory; against the 4B played the same way it wrote 1.7 times as fast and held under half the memory. Its earlier model, the 4B, is its fallback.

snapdragon-x2.label: Snapdragon X2 Elite / X2 Plus (Hexagon v81)

pluginPatch.what: Castellan's build of GenieX 0.8.0's llama.cpp plugin: qualcomm/GenieX v0.8.0 with three commits of Castellan's (kit node/geniex/README.md), signed with Castellan's certificate. snapdragon-x2.basis: Measured on the X2 Elite with Qwen3-VL-2B Q4_0 (--compute npu --nctx 2560, GENIEX_IMAGE_MAX_TOKENS 1024, 2026-10-18, on a private port in the NPU's turn), GenieX 0.9.1's own plugin against this build: after a chat, a 3.27 GB working set, 0.73 GB private and 3.21 GB on the NPU against 1.62, 0.25 and 1.50; after a picture, 3.21 GB on the NPU against 2.45, and 75 quiet seconds later 3.21 against 1.52 (its encoder freed), the PC's available memory 3.6 GB lower against 1.6; its first answer after a start in 3.5 s against 4.7. Its pictures as 0.9.1's own: 34 of 35 screen questions at 1,024 picture tokens in a median 1.50 s, 21 of 21 questions about ten photos in 1.45 s, npu-bench's four pictures right in a median 278 ms; chat at 72.5 tokens written a second, and 21 of 24 quality items, every must-pass one right, as 0.9.1's own. Its threads (kit 2.98.1): GenieX's plugin starts 18 threads on the X2 Elite for the few operations the NPU leaves to the processor, and at ggml's default (poll 50) they spin through each token. Eight chats, about 1,200 tokens written at 72.3 tokens a second, kept 5.12 of the processor's cores busy and drew 699 mJ a token over the PC at rest; with poll 0, 0.05 cores and 251 mJ, at 72.9 tokens a second (2026-10-22, Windows' Energy Meter counters as npu-bench reads them, spec/NPU-BENCHMARK.md). Its context is 4,096 tokens with 512-token micro-batches (-c 4096 -ub 512, 2026-10-15): 1.4 GB on the NPU and a 2.0 GB working set, against 2.9 and 4.4 GB at -c 8192 -ub 2048, in the same time and to the same vectors (cosine 0.99999 or more). Its cap, 1,365 by the kit's estimate of 3 characters a token, keeps a request under 4,096 real tokens at one a character; a longer one would be refused (400)

rerankServer.basis: Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B Q8_0 (setup's reranker) on llama.cpp b11645 over GenieX 0.9.3's libraries, measured on a Snapdragon X2 Elite Extreme (Hexagon v81, 48 GB) on 2026-10-23 with Reeve's own 24 rerank queries (its ten best files, 1,600 characters each). Its order matched the Adreno's reranker (b11734, OpenCL) as closely as the processor's does: where they differed, the files swapped were near-ties (10 pairs in 24 queries, each within 0.0074 of each other; the first file in 3 queries, within 0.0012; the processor swapped 12, up to 0.051 apart), and the accuracy was the same: blended with search's order, the right file first for 12 of 24 and in the top five for 19 (words alone: 8 and 18). A ten-file rerank took 849 ms (median; 943 at p90), against 1,558 on the Adreno and 2,286 on the processor. It holds 1.10 GB of the NPU's memory at -c 4096 -ub 512, against 1.65 GB at the cards' -c 8192 -ub 2048, at the same speed. In the NPU's turn, as the manor runs it, GenieX's chat writes beside it at the same speed (73.2 tokens a second, 73.3 without it): a chat waits for at most one rerank (about 0.85 s), and a rerank waited 0.19 s for a chat (median; 1.5 s at most). Asked at the same moment, outside the turn, a rerank slows a chat about five times, so it always takes the NPU's turn.

meteor-lake.label: Core Ultra Series 1, 200U or 200H, Meteor Lake or Arrow Lake-U or -H (NPU 3720)
meteor-lake.basis: Measured by the NPU check on Intel Core Ultra 5 225U (Arrow Lake-U, whose NPU 3720 shows Meteor Lake's 7D1D), NPU driver 32.0.100.5540, 2026-10-14, every step passing, the prompt read 128 tokens at a time: writes 10.1 tokens a second: 200 ms a token allows twice that; reading 1550 tokens took 6.4 s: a 15 s base allows twice that and a warm answer. OpenVINO's own 1,024-token chunks cost every prompt a whole chunk: a short answer 3.1 s against 0.5, two at once 6.4 s against 1.2, 1,550 tokens 7.0 s against 4.0 to 6.4. Then 20 quick benchmarks on the same PC (npu-bench, 2026-10-14), each also reading prompts no cache had seen: in 64-token chunks a short answer took 0.35 s and 1,740 tokens 8.1 s; in 128, 0.5 s and 6.3 s; in 256, 0.78 s and 6.0 s; in 512, 1.43 s and 6.4 s; in 1,024, 3.1 s and 6.9 s: 128, for Qwen3-4B. Kit 2.103.0's Qwen3-VL-2B (INT8) on the same PC, 2026-10-23, with BEST_PERF and the prefix cache off: in 128-token chunks a short answer took 0.3 to 0.6 s, 1,805 tokens 4.3 to 4.4 s and a 236-token picture 2.0 s; in 256, 0.5 to 0.7 s, 3.8 to 3.9 s and 1.8 s; in 512, 0.9 to 1.2 s, 3.7 to 3.8 s and 2.2 s; in OpenVINO's 1,024, 1.9 to 2.5 s, 3.9 s and 3.5 s: 256, its long prompts and pictures a tenth quicker than in 128 for a tenth of a second on a short answer. GENERATE_HINT BEST_PERF writes 12.3 to 13.1 tokens a second against 9.3 to 11.2, and the benchmark's jobs took 27.3 to 28.0 s against 29.1 to 35.6 (castellan-npu-bench/2, whose prompts no cache has seen, 2026-10-15), the same reads and answers; it doubles the first compile, 56.5 to 68.7 s against 25.8 to 28.9: the slowest start to a first answer took 69 s: 120 s allows half again. OpenVINO Model Server turns the NPU's prefix caching on: at the benchmark's end the server held 5.98 GB with its 128 blocks of 128 tokens, 4.30 GB with 32, and 3.72 GB with the cache off, which also read 2 to 5% faster and did the jobs in 27.25 to 27.48 s against 27.67 to 28.01 with 32 blocks (two runs each). The agents' prompts share 25 to 90 tokens at their start, less than a block, so a cache is hardly ever hit: the route's command turns it off (--enable_prefix_caching false: --plugin_config can't, OpenVINO Model Server refusing its key there as doubled), and 3.8 GB for the 4B. The 2B holds 2.9 GB loaded and 4.8 once it has read a full-size screenshot (1,024 tokens, 12 to 15 s: OpenVINO GenAI runs a picture's encoder on the processor beside an NPU, and it keeps what that took), 5.0 at its peak; with the embeddings on the graphics beside it (1.1 to 1.3 GB), the two took 5.8 GB of the PC's available memory, twice over: chat 4.9 and embeddings 1.3, which a 16 GB PC's budget holds. The encoder on the graphics (AUTO's MULTI_DEVICE_PRIORITIES GPU) read a full-size screenshot in 6 to 7 s, but read an 896 by 896 picture's 4827 as 4877 three times in four, which the processor read right every time, and at INFERENCE_PRECISION_HINT f32 answered nonsense: it stays on the processor. PREFILL_HINT STATIC read every prompt in 7.4 s; NPU_TURBO was no faster, and STATIC prefill attention read 15 to 20% slower. A 3,072-token prompt held the 4B 0.4 GB more and read 5 to 10% slower; a 4,096-token one 1.0 GB more, past a 16 GB PC's room for chat and embeddings together (the 2B at 4,096 in 512-token chunks: 0.6 GB more). Its embeddings run on the processor's graphics (embedArgs), measured on the same PC's Intel Graphics, 2026-10-15, two runs each, the same model and command started by hand: a query in 49 to 50 ms against the NPU's 1.13 s, 16 of Reeve's chunks in 4.8 s against 18.0, a dense one (1,100 to 1,320 tokens) in 0.73 to 0.95 s against 2.5, the NPU's vectors (cosine 0.997 to 0.999), and 1.25 GB of the PC's memory against 1.14 to 1.18. Beside the chat server with this command, chat wrote 13.1 to 13.3 tokens a second while the graphics indexed, as alone, against 6.5 to 6.8 with both on the NPU. The NPU at --max_length 512 answered a query in 0.27 s but refused Reeve's dense chunks; the processor slowed chat by a fifth and took 2.3 GB.

arrow-lake.label: Core Ultra 200S or 200HX, Arrow Lake-S or -HX (NPU 3720)
arrow-lake.basis: Not measured: the NPU 3720 measured under meteor-lake, with its prompt settings and memory; the generous starting values stay until the NPU check runs on one.

lunar-lake.label: Core Ultra 200V, Lunar Lake (NPU 4)
lunar-lake.basis: Measured by the NPU check on a Lunar Lake (Core Ultra 7 256V), 2026-10-12, with OpenVINO's own prompt settings and prefix cache: the route's timeouts and cap, with Qwen3-4B (the route's memory is the 2B's on the NPU 3720 at 4,096 tokens: the route's notes). Its prompt settings are estimated from the NPU 3720 (meteor-lake), the only other Intel NPU there is to run (NPU-VENDORS.md, Estimated): the NPU 4 read a 1,024-token chunk in 0.23 to 0.26 of the NPU 3720's time, and a chunk costs a fixed part and a part for each of its tokens. In 512-token chunks a short prompt should take 0.3 to 0.4 s, what the NPU 3720 takes in its 128, against 0.72 s in OpenVINO's 1,024, and the jobs' prompts 18 to 27% less, whether or not the fixed part is faster on the NPU 4. The NPU 3720 at this 4,096-token prompt bears it out: in 512-token chunks it read about 3,500 tokens in 12.9 to 13.3 s, against 15.0 to 15.8 in 128 and 16.2 to 16.6 in 1,024. GENERATE_HINT BEST_PERF wrote 30% faster there for about twice the first compile (80 to 90 s against 42): 31 to 41 s here, so about 60 to 90 s, inside the 180 s cold load. The prefix cache is off, as on every Intel NPU (the route's command, meteor-lake): the agents' prompts share too little to hit it, and at 4,096 tokens on the NPU 3720 it held 0.4 to 0.6 GB more, read no faster, and at OpenVINO's default 128 blocks grew to 6.17 GB.

panther-lake.label: Core Ultra Series 3, Panther Lake (NPU 5)
panther-lake.basis: Not measured: NPU 5 at 50 TOPS, about the Lunar Lake's NPU 4 (48), so its values and its estimated prompt settings (lunar-lake), with room for a newer compiler's first compile; setup measures each PC.

wildcat-lake.label: Core Series 3, Wildcat Lake (NPU 5)
wildcat-lake.basis: Not measured: Panther Lake's NPU 5, but a third of it, 15 to 17 TOPS against 50, about 1.4 times the NPU 3720's 11.5, so the NPU 3720's prompt settings and memory (meteor-lake): a 512-token chunk would take it 0.9 s, a 128-token one 0.3 s (NPU-VENDORS.md, Estimated). It goes in low-cost laptops of 8 to 16 GB, where the NPU 3720's 2,048-token prompt leaves room for the embedding server and 4,096 doesn't. Panther Lake's starting timeouts, with room for a newer compiler's first compile; setup measures each PC.

models.licence: Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct: Apache-2.0; Castellan-AI's symmetric INT8 export of it carries the base model's licence, with its LICENSE and a note of what was changed

idleStop.basis: The slowest measured, rounded up to a tenth of a second: npu-check --idle on the NPU 3720 (Core Ultra 5 225U, 2026-10-15), every step passing, its servers stopped by the keeper after a minute unused and woken by a person's request: chat started to its first answer in 6.85 s, embeddings in 2.74 s, from the compile cache (--cache_dir). On a Lunar Lake chat started in 4 s (2026-10-12), and its embeddings weren't timed apart. The first compile (31 to 41 s there, about a minute on an NPU 3720 with BEST_PERF) is once per PC and model, not per start. 20 times either cold start is under 5 minutes, so 5.
idleStop.verify: Run on the NPU 3720 (2026-10-15); still to run on a Lunar Lake laptop with 16 GB (Windows shows 15.3 to 15.9), with OpenVINO Model Server set up by setup: stop the manor's own NPU servers first (or let the keeper stop them), then run node <agent>\src\kit\npu-check.ts --idle --yes from any agent that has the kit (2.71.0 or later). It starts the chat and embedding servers through the kit, has the keeper stop both once the NPU has been unused a minute (idle-stop: their processes gone, the memory freed said), asks again as a person would with a 20 s timeout (idle-cold-answer: told the local AI is waking, answered within the cold load; the time is this PC's cold start), and checks a request in flight is never stopped (idle-in-flight). It passes or fails each step and prints the idleStop numbers its cold start gives; if they differ from these, change coldStartMs and minutes here.

intel.embeddings: on the NPU, through a second OpenVINO Model Server of its own (one process serves one task from the command line): OpenVINO's channel-wise INT4 Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B, last-token pooling, compiled for 2,048 tokens. The NPU compiles a fixed shape, so every request costs the full 2,048 and a longer one is refused (400); a dense 1,500-character chunk (UUIDs, hex, base64) is up to 1,338 tokens, so 1,024 wouldn't do. Its cap, 680 by the kit's estimate of 3 characters a token, keeps a request under 2,048 real tokens at nearly one a character. Measured on a Lunar Lake 2026-10-13: the graphics card's own results (OpenVINO, the same model), a query in 166 ms and 16 of Reeve's chunks in 2.6 s, against 5.9 s on the Arc through llama.cpp's Vulkan build, which setup gives the card

model.licence: Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B: Apache-2.0 (OpenVINO's channel-wise INT4 export of it)

pluginPatch.what: Castellan's build of OpenVINO GenAI 2026.4.1.0's openvino_genai.dll: openvinotoolkit/openvino.genai at tag 2026.4.1.0 with two fixes of Castellan's (kit node/openvino/README.md), signed with Castellan's certificate. A prompt without a picture to Qwen3-VL no longer crashes on the NPU, and a request that fails part-way no longer makes every later one fail until the server restarts
pluginPatch.required: Qwen3-VL, the route's model for chat and pictures, fails on the NPU with OpenVINO GenAI 2026.4.1's own: a prompt without a picture crashes (roi_end <= max_dim), and once one request has failed every later one does (prompt_ids.get_size() >= tokenized_history.size()) until the server restarts
pluginPatch.basis: Built on the Core Ultra 5 225U, 2026-10-23, from tag 2026.4.1.0 (ab01d1771e4, the version OpenVINO Model Server 2026.4.1 carries) against OpenVINO 2026.4.1 from pip, with Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools (node/openvino/build-openvino-genai.bat): all 201 functions ovms.exe takes from it are there. Its stock pin is the file OpenVINO Model Server 2026.4.1's zip carries, and needs the OpenVINO runtime it links against, as that zip carries it. Measured there on the NPU 3720 with Castellan-AI/Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct-int8-sym-ov: with the server's own file every prompt without a picture failed; with this build npu-bench's full run answered 22 of 24 and 4 of 4 pictures. It's 7.5 MB, too big for every agent's kit to carry, so setup downloads it from Manor-releases, checked against its size and SHA-256

retired.why: Castellan's channel-wise INT4 export of Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507, the route's model, text only, until Qwen3-VL-2B took its place in kit 2.103.0. A PC still set up with it (its local AI not set up since, or the 2B failed setup's test there) runs it, and its entry names it, so it stays there.

intel.notes: A zip, unpacked into the tools home: no installer, no administrator. Its programs need the Microsoft Visual C++ runtime, which its zip doesn't carry (only its Python's vcruntime140): setup copies the five DLLs they import from Microsoft's own CRT package (runtime, pinned) beside ovms.exe, where Windows loads them first, so no administrator installs the Redistributable (run on a Lunar Lake, 2026-10-12). It needs Intel's NPU driver 32.0.100.4023 or later. It serves the OpenAI routes at /v1 (and the older /v3), source-checked at v2026.4.1. The NPU compiles a model on first load (minutes), cached in --cache_dir. Its zip wraps everything in an ovms folder, which setup unpacks into ovms-2026.4.1; its Python (for chat templates) needs PYTHONHOME and PATH, which the entry's env gives (its setupvars script does the same). Its model (kit 2.103.0) is one for chat and pictures, Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct, as Castellan exported it to symmetric INT8 (optimum-cli export openvino --weight-format int8 --sym; its model card has the versions) and publishes it as Castellan-AI/Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct-int8-sym-ov: its pictures capped at 1,048,576 px, 1,024 tokens, in its own configs (pictureTokens, so the kit fits a larger one the same), its files pinned for every generation (each PC compiles it for its own NPU). It runs only on Castellan's build of OpenVINO GenAI (pluginPatch; kit/node/openvino/README.md): with the server's own, every prompt without a picture fails on the NPU. Its symmetric INT4 export answered "Yes" to "Reply with the single word: ready" every time. Its language model has Qwen3-VL's three DeepStack steps rewritten into transformers' own form (scatter_deepstack.py, in its repository): NPUW recognises only that form, and with optimum-intel's masked add it zeroed those features on the NPU, which misread clear text the processor read right. The full benchmark on a Core Ultra 5 225U (NPU 3720) at its generation's settings, 2026-10-23: 22 of 24 answers, 4 of 4 pictures, 17.9 tokens written a second, the three jobs in 12.9 s against the Qwen3-4B's 27.4; a full-size screenshot 12 to 15 s, its encoder on the processor (meteor-lake). Until kit 2.103.0 the route ran Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507, text only, as Castellan's channel-wise INT4 export (Castellan-AI/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507-int4-cw-ov): a group-wise AWQ export, OpenVINO's Qwen3-4B-int4-ov, answers nonsense on a Lunar Lake NPU ("?option?option…") and properly on its processor and graphics card (2026-10-12). The route's timeouts and cap are the Lunar Lake's with it (Core Ultra 7 256V, NPU driver 32.0.100.4512): at --max_prompt_len 4096 (the NPU check, 2026-10-13, every step passed) the first load 41 s; a short answer warm in 0.8 s, 24 to 28 tokens written a second; 3,112 tokens read in 4.6 s; 3,827 answered and 4,352 refused plainly (400), the server still up; 4.3 GB working set. The bigger compile cost a short prompt about 70 ms against 1,536 tokens, and the benchmark's jobs nothing. The 2B at 4,096 tokens on the NPU 3720 (512-token chunks) answered a 1,805-token prompt and full-size screenshots, holding 5.5 GB after them, 0.6 more than at 2,048: chat's 5.5 GB here. Its embedding server beside it (embedServer) adds 1.7 GB; the two run on the NPU at once where there's room: a 32 GB PC's 12.4 GB for the NPU holds both, a 16 GB one's 6.2 no longer does with the 2B (7.2), so setup leaves the embeddings to the graphics card there.

xdna.label: Ryzen 7040/8040, Phoenix and Hawk Point (XDNA)
xdna.why: no NPU model server runs language models on the first XDNA NPU (Lemonade's FAQ: none plans to)

xdna2.label: Ryzen AI 300 and later: Strix Point, Krackan, Strix Halo, Gorgon Point (XDNA 2)
xdna2.basis: Measured by the NPU check on AMD Ryzen AI 7 350 w/ Radeon 860M (Krackan, 16 GB), NPU driver 32.0.20102.3930, 2026-10-15, Qwen3.5-2B for chat and vision, its context 4,096 (--ctx-len), every measuring step passing: writes 19.4 tokens a second: 150 ms a token allows twice that; reading 3,272 tokens took 4.1 s: a 15 s base allows twice that and a warm answer; the slowest start to a first answer took 17 s (the kit's test request, a picture and then chat): 30 s allows half again. One model answers chat and pictures, so nothing switches between them. Qwen3-4B's, before it: writes 13.8 tokens a second, 3,115 tokens read in 6.6 s, a 20 s base, and its switch to and from its vision model, 8 to 9 s, inside each.

powerTool.broken: an older AMD NPU driver left its files in Windows\System32\AMD, where AMD's xrt-smi.exe loads them and can't start, and FastFlowLM sets the power mode with xrt-smi. Removing that older driver package fixes it (an administrator's job, with pnputil /delete-driver)

idleStop.basis: The slowest measured, rounded up to a tenth of a second, Qwen3.5-2B for chat and vision. Chat: npu-check --idle on a Ryzen AI 7 350 (Krackan, 16 GB), 2026-10-15, every step passing: stopped to its first answer in 15.0 s (FastFlowLM loads the model before it opens its port), the keeper's stop freeing 3.7 GB. Vision: the NPU check's kit-test the same day, the kit's test request on a stopped server, a picture and then chat, 16.5 s: the same server and model, so no switch. Started alike from Node, three times each, Qwen3.5-2B answered first in 11.8 to 12.4 s and Qwen3-4B in 10.1 to 10.7 s; Qwen3-4B's idleStop was 6.6 s for chat and 15.7 s for vision (its switch to the vision model, 9.2 s, included). All of these were measured while Reeve embedded on the Radeon 860M, which shares the PC's memory with the NPU: Qwen3-4B's server came up in 8.5 to 9.3 s then, against 4 to 6 s on the quiet PC that gave its 6.6 s, so they are on the slow side.
idleStop.verify: On a Ryzen AI 300 (XDNA 2) laptop with 16 GB, with FastFlowLM set up by setup: stop the manor's own NPU server first (or let the keeper stop it), then run node <agent>\src\kit\npu-check.ts --idle --yes from any agent that has the kit (2.71.0 or later). It passes or fails each step and prints the idleStop numbers its cold start gives; if they differ from these, change coldStartMs and minutes here.

amd.embeddings: not on the NPU: FastFlowLM's embedding model is EmbeddingGemma, under Gemma's terms; embeddings go to the graphics card or the processor
amd.licence: FastFlowLM: MIT (orchestration and CLI), NPU kernels free for any use including commercial; asks for "Powered by FastFlowLM" in the product's notices

offNpu.basis: Qwen3.5-2B, the model FastFlowLM runs on the NPU, as unsloth's Q4_0 GGUF and F16 projector (Hugging Face, unsloth/Qwen3.5-2B-GGUF at f6d5376b, Apache-2.0), run by llama.cpp b11734 on the Radeon (its Vulkan build) and on the processor (its x64 build), at FastFlowLM's --ctx-len 4096 and with its thinking off, as FastFlowLM serves it. FastFlowLM's own weights are in its NPU format (q4nx), which nothing else reads: Q4_0 is the nearest 4-bit GGUF. Downloaded into the tools home's models folder (1.9 GB), for the benchmark only.

amd.notes: A portable zip, unpacked into the tools home: no installer, no administrator. AMD's NPU driver 32.0.203.311 or later (an administrator installs drivers). One server holds one model: Qwen3.5-2B answers chat and pictures alike, so nothing switches (the Qwen3-4B pair before it, one model for chat and one for vision, took 8 to 9 s to switch either way). Models are kept in %USERPROFILE%\.flm\models. Its context is --ctx-len 4096, the cap: FastFlowLM holds its whole context on the NPU from the start, and without it took the model's own, 40,960 tokens for Qwen3-4B (about 144 KB a token, 5.6 GB, on top of 3.3 GB of weights). On a Ryzen AI 7 350 with 16 GB, where Windows lets a device hold half the PC's memory at once (7.6 GB), that never loaded (XRT 0xc01e0200, the video memory manager couldn't page every allocation in at once), from a fresh start too; at 4,096 Qwen3-4B loaded in 4 to 6 s and held 4.5 GB, at 8,192 10.6 s and 5.1 GB, at the same speed (13.9 to 14.1 tokens a second), and its vision model held 5.3 GB. Qwen3.5-2B at 4,096 holds 3.7 GB started and 4.0 to 4.1 GB after jobs and pictures, writes 19.4 to 21.0 tokens a second and reads about 800. Its tokenizer has 248,320 entries against Qwen3's 151,936, so the same text is usually fewer tokens to it, and the kit's estimate of 3 characters a token stays on the safe side. FastFlowLM serves it with its thinking off. A failed load doesn't stop it: it serves on, /v1/models listing every model it knows, and answers each request 200 with only {"error":"Failed to load … model!"} (it tries the load again each time); the kit takes that for the server failing (failedWithOk), and the NPU check asks /api/ps, which lists the model it holds (reportsLoaded). A prompt past its context is refused 400 ("Max length reached!"), the server still up. Its power mode: at each start FastFlowLM runs C:\Windows\System32\AMD\xrt-smi.exe configure --pmode (performance by default) and ignores the result. On the Krackan that never ran: an older driver's xrt_coreutil.dll (2024) beside the newer xrt-smi.exe lacks a function it needs, so xrt-smi failed to load at every start (silently from Node, which the kit starts it from; with a dialog for each start from anywhere else). So its --pmode runs (powersaver, balanced, performance, turbo: the same speed on mains power, 14.0 tokens a second each, and on battery, none drawing clearly less than the battery meter's own swing) all ran in one mode, the driver's own, and say nothing of the modes: the route sets none until they're measured on a PC whose xrt-smi runs. With Qwen3-4B, in that one mode, on battery it used 20.7 mJ a token (npu-bench --energy), wrote 13.1 tokens a second and loaded in 12.7 s (5.4 s on mains power), and a smaller --prefill-chunk-len than its 4,096 only read slower (3,000 tokens 7.3 s at 1,024, 9.5 s at 512, against 5.3 s). It reads far faster than it writes: Qwen3-4B 34 to 36 times (472 to 512 tokens a second read, 13.1 to 14.4 written, on mains power and on battery), Qwen3.5-2B 41 times (795 and 19.4), so readPerWrite is 30: on a generation nobody has measured, calibrate takes a full-cap read at 30 times the writing speed it measured (the Krackan's --harden measurement gave a 35 s base with Qwen3-4B and 25 s with Qwen3.5-2B, where the kit's 10 gave 90 s). Its --img-pre-resize default (2: a large picture scaled to a height of 720; a small one isn't enlarged) is kept, measured with Qwen3-4B's vision model: a 1920x1080 screen cost 960 tokens and 4.5 s an answer and a 1080x2400 phone screen 270 tokens and 2.3 s, every answer right, where the original size cost 2,080 and 2,600 tokens and twice to four times the time for nothing more right, and a height of 480 misread small text. FastFlowLM 1.0.7 misreads a picture it doesn't shrink (720 px tall or less) when a side is a whole number of 32 px, so the route has the quirk sides-of-32: the kit makes such a side a pixel longer before sending it (NPU-VENDORS.md, FastFlowLM's pictures with sides of 32 px). It keeps no prefix cache: a request asked again costs the same. It streams a token a chunk, with its usage in the last (stream_options.include_usage).
